prize_parts.citation: for the conception and leadership of IceCube and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, opening neutrino astronomy
for the optical lattice clock and its development to 10^-18 precision

statement.case_for: I ranked B037 first because the experimental Higgs discovery is the most central finding in the list, but the discussion has shown me that the case rests on a principled choice among thousands of collaborators that this committee has not made. The pairing of B002 and B022 is cleaner. IceCube is a genuinely new window on the universe: a diffuse TeV-PeV astrophysical flux, then the TXS 0506+056 blazar and the Galactic plane, from a detector concept many thought unrealistic. The optical lattice clock is a discovery-plus-instrument story in which Katori's magic-wavelength idea and Ye's push to 10^-18 are separable and complementary, independently reproduced and now bearing on tests of constants, geodesy and the redefinition of the second. The two are distinct achievements, each with unusually well-defined credit, and together use exactly three names.
statement.case_against: B002 gives a single name for a large collaboration; Halzen is the conceiver and long-term leader, but AMANDA colleagues and the analysis teams are left out, and the source identification is still incomplete. Pairing it with the clocks makes a prize spanning astroparticle physics and precision metrology, which could look like a convenience pairing rather than a unifying theme. And I am setting aside B037, which I still regard as the most fundamental discovery, because of an attribution difficulty rather than a scientific one.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks at 10^-18 realise the principle that progress is set by what can be measured, with Katori and Ye a natural two-person prize and the redefinition of the second pending.
responses.response: I agree on the merit and on the clean attribution, and it moved me towards a prize that includes B022. I do not agree that it should stand alone as the first-ranked case. The consequences for fundamental physics are mostly still prospective, tests of constants and dark-matter signatures so far give bounds rather than discoveries, so I would weigh it as a strong instrument prize and pair it with something that is a discovery in the strict sense.

responses.point: IceCube's detection of a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux and the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane opened neutrino astronomy; Halzen is the sole credited name as conceiver and leader.
responses.response: I share this view, which is why B002 is in my configuration. I want to qualify one point: a single name for a collaboration of hundreds works only if the committee accepts that the conception of a cubic-kilometre detector and its decades of leadership is the decisive contribution. I would want the external experts to confirm the AMANDA to IceCube history before we rely on that, and I would not accept the Galactic-plane result as part of the citation, since it is recent.

responses.point: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B028) is original, with a clean theory plus experiment pairing of Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and opens moire quantum materials.
responses.response: I take this seriously and keep B028 as an alternative, since it has the broadest support in the room. My reservation is maturity: the 2018 experiments are still being absorbed and the nature of the superconductivity is unsettled. The credit also leaves out Cao and the first-author experimental team, and Bistritzer's inclusion makes three names that would consume the entire prize. I would favour waiting for the interpretation to stabilise.

responses.point: Circuit QED (B014) is foundational for superconducting processors and distinct from the 2025 prize, with Blais, Schoelkopf and Wallraff as the coherent trio.
responses.response: I find this impressive technologically, but placing it directly after the 2025 award on superconducting circuits risks the appearance of repeating the same area, and Girvin's omission from your trio would be a real injustice given his role in the 2004 theory. I would not put it in the preferred configuration this year.

responses.point: The Higgs discovery through ATLAS and CMS (B037) fills a conspicuous gap after the 2013 theory prize, but honouring a few leaders over thousands is contentious.
responses.response: You state the difficulty more honestly than I did in my opening. I still think it is the most important physics on the list and I keep it as my first alternative, but I now think we would need a clear principle, for example the founding architects of the detectors, before it can carry a prize, and I do not see that we have agreed on one.

uncertainties: Whether Halzen alone adequately represents the decisive credit for IceCube, and how AMANDA and collaboration leadership should be treated.
Whether the committee can agree a principle for crediting detector architects for B037, which would change my first choice.
Whether a two-part prize spanning neutrino astronomy and optical clocks is judged coherent.
I rely on general knowledge for the formal roles of credited people.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile: my work in string theory, cosmology and black-hole physics, my PhD under David Gross and my Uppsala group do not connect to any of the shortlisted candidates.
